added_failures_note: The reviewed run recorded no baseline_suite or after_suite (both null in its classification.json; the keys are absent from its manifest), so it carries no two-arm suite delta of its own. Its own gate log (runs/r-20261019T035327482346-ssog-anchor-family-runner/runner-heuristic.log) ends EXIT=0 and its arm JSON records outcome_status complete with containment holds, and its gate was its own instrument (ruff, py_compile and --self-check-containment on four planted inputs, all matching), not pytest; the change touches only docs/evidence paths that no test module covers, so the added-failure set is empty rather than unmeasured by a suite that could have exercised it.

findings.text: follow-on: LOG_DIR's default embeds this dispatch's reckon run id (r-20261019T035327482346-ssog-anchor-family-runner), a transient identifier the run-record GC removes, so a later arm for any other of the nine families in selection.json writes its apply log into a directory that may no longer exist, and the runner's log location is pinned to one past dispatch rather than to the arm being run.

follow-on: the post-apply budget test compares spend against ARM_BUDGET_USD (2.00) while the cap handed to harmonize is apply_cap() (1.98 for a three-call family), so an arm that spent between 1.98 and 2.00 would be recorded complete though it exceeded the limit the runner itself passed to the apply.

follow-on: the containment check has no test -- a grep of tests/ finds no reference to evaluate_containment or self_check_containment -- so its only guard is a flag a caller must remember to pass, and an edit that weakened either control would stay green in the default gate.
